criteria.C1: open machine-readable access with timestamp, type and point coordinates
criteria.C2: a type naming street/surface flooding, separate from basement, sewer-backup and catch-basin types
criteria.C3: >= 1 reserve-period day (>= 2022-01-01) with >= 50 such reports city-wide (rain311 event rule); DEV days are a bonus
criteria.C4: no licence term forbidding research use

note: C3 first required a DEV day too; relaxed to reserve-only after New Orleans was seen (its 2019+ system has no DEV day), because the owner's aim is reserve diversity. Recorded in R30.

new_orleans.note: 2012-2018 archive (3iz8-nghx) has only a merged 'Street Flooding/Drainage' type: fails C2, not used

flood_types: SubType 'Flooding or Standing Water for Days' (2025-)
miami_dade.note: 2024 layer needs a token (not used); 2025+ Subject 'Flooding or Drainage Issue' mixes drainage: fails C2, not used

baltimore.why: C3: 'WW-Storm Flooded Street' exists (8,451 reports 2011-2026) but no reserve day >= 50 (max 65 on 2015-06-27)

washington_dc.why: C3 (max 10/day, 612 reports); C2 also doubtful: 'DC Water - Customer Flooding' / 'Emergency - Flooding'

boston.why: C3: 'Roadway Flooding' only since 2024 (17 in 2024, 220 in 2025); no day >= 50

los_angeles.why: C2: MyLA311 has no flooding type

detroit.why: C2: only blocked catch basin / water main / basement types

houston.why: C1: no 311 request data on data.houstontx.gov (only a knowledge-base dump)

toronto.why: C1: 311 service requests have no point coordinates (ward / postal prefix / intersection names only)
